reading_story leans on a generic wedding trope (ring onto bride's finger, sun crowns their marriage), reducing distinctiveness from neighboring 女/日 kanji, though it stays within gates.

reading_story: Jitter shakes the War Helmet loose, spills the Starfish out from under the Thatched House roof — proof this whole scene is REALITY, not a dream.

Reading_story reuses 'crushed Mound of Soil' and repeats the keyword HARM, a minor redundancy but not disqualifying.

story: DRAW NEAR: beneath the Thatched House's roof, a Starfish clings halfway down the wall, arms reaching, while the Approval Stamp thunks the doorstep below, marking YES for every traveler who approaches.
reading_story: Key twirls between his fingers as visitors DRAW NEAR, and he presses it into the lock the instant they arrive.

story: WEALTH: the Thatched House shelters an Open Mouth gorging on endless grain from the brimming Rice-Paddy Grid below — the whole home swells fat with riches.

story: Inside the thatched house, a wellhead grid straddles the horizon line; below it a wishbone cracks apart, and one ink droplet freezes solid on the floor — brutally COLD.

story: Under the Thatched House's roof, a Rubber Glove points up at the Crescent Moon, using hand signals to show what tomorrow's weather will be — nothing but a GUESS.

story: A SENTENCE stands printed on the left page; facing it on the right, the Tape Measure unspools itself, tongue quivering, stretching to match it line for line, mirror for mirror. OPPOSITE.
reading_story: Ty Cobb slides in hard, clipped and short, straight at the catcher blocking home plate — two men OPPOSITE, neither giving ground.

story: In a cramped BUREAU, a Draped Cloak slumps behind the desk, its hood gaping into an Open Mouth that barks stamps-and-forms orders at the line.

story: RESIDE here forever: a limp Draped Cloak droops over an OLD wooden chair, folding down like a body gone slack, settling into that ancient seat it never once leaves.

issues: Minor (non-gating): in reading_story, RESIDE falls mid-sentence (word 5 of 21) rather than at start/end; acceptable since the main story anchors the keyword at start and the reading story's governing gate is reading-actor presence.

story: Falling Katana slashes clean between the Woolly Ram's fleece and the I-Beam Girder below — one clearly wool, one clearly steel: an unmistakable DISTINCTION.
reading_story: Sah measures the gap the katana cut, calling out each DISTINCTION between ram and girder in one short breath.

story: Under the clamped-down Pot Lid, a Hanging Towel sways above rows of stalls — welcome to the CITY market square.
reading_story: Sheriff patrols the stalls beneath the Pot Lid roof, badge gleaming, keeping peace across the whole CITY.

story: Under a Bedsheet Cover, three Bean Sprouts poke up every single day, always into the same yawning Open Mouth, above the same Hanging Towel drying in its USUAL spot — nothing ever changes.

story: The ANTENNA MAST leans level, resting its long bar across the Twin Pillars' shared ledge — perfectly balanced, perfectly FLAT.
reading_story: Hayes surveys the flat plain and declares it FLAT — level ground fit for any building.

issues: Non-blocking: 'HAPPINESS floods me' and 'planted proud' lean slightly on abstract/emotive framing rather than pure visual, but the surrounding image is concrete enough that meaning still lands.
Non-blocking: reading_story uses standard runner props (finish line, gold medal, chest) — appropriate scene-building for the Coe persona, not phantom components.

story: Dozens of pale Silk Cocoons snag along the Barbed Pike's hooked spur, spilling down its upright shaft. An open Stepladder stands planted at its foot — HOW MANY cocoons hang there?
reading_story: The terse locksmith cuts a fresh Key, holds it to the light, and clips out one question — HOW MANY teeth does this blank still need?
issues: Minor (non-blocking): the Stepladder is spatially placed at the pike's foot but plays no active role in the scene, slightly weakening its own encoding vs. the cocoon/pike pairing.

story: Beneath the Cliff Awning's slanted shade, an open Stepladder stands firmly on the Mound of Soil, its flat step packed with dirt into a rough squatting CUSHION.
reading_story: Zah settles onto the packed-dirt mound, wriggling until it molds to his hips, sighing contentedly on his makeshift CUSHION.
issues: All three mandatory components (广 Cliff Awning, 土 Mound of Soil, 人 Stepladder) are named with personas intact; no phantom components.

No etymology is invoked; word counts (~27 and ~20 words) are well under the 40-word cap.

reading_story: Tay strolls through the palace COURTYARD, tossing coins into a splashing fountain and laughing softly beneath the flowering trees.

reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer poses just so, her silhouette taking perfect SHAPE under the spotlight.

reading_story: Yakker barks roll call at the barracks gate, listing every man's DUTY for the war campaign -- yak, yak, yak, his voice cracks like a whip.

reading_story: Toker counts his GAIN in short, clipped puffs — 'toku, toku' — never taking more than his measured share.

reading_story: The Hitcher hitchhikes with a knife-scarred HEART pinned to his jacket — CERTAIN proof of the ride that marked him.

Reading story keyword 'FORGETs' sits mid-sentence rather than start/end; acceptable here since the entire reading scene (freezing, mouthing nothing) is thematically the forgetting, but placement is slightly buried.
Meaning-story payoff 'forget my own name' is inherently abstract/invisible, which caps imageability; the concrete anchors are only 'slumps' and 'stare down'.

story: The Twin Candle Wicks stand on their left ledge, each flame stretching sideways to light a hundred tiny birthday candles at once, guttering wildly, far too BUSY to hold still.
reading_story: Backstage, Bowie zips between costume racks in a lightning-bolt jumpsuit, missing three cues, moaning that a world tour keeps a Starman impossibly BUSY.

story: Living only in the NOW, no memory of past or future, this HEART obsesses over one single WISH, over and over.
reading_story: Nenn kneels before his HEART's shrine, chanting the same WISH again and again — Nenn only ever prays for the now.

issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword ANGRY is followed by a trailing action clause ('chasing the boy round the couch'); it remains the capitalized climactic payoff so it is not buried, but the payoff is crispest in the main story where ANGRY is the final word.
Note (non-gating): 奴 appears in phonetic_extra and is correctly used only as the source of reading actor Doh (ど), not as a component — no coverage or phantom problem.

reading_story: Foo, the darting Foo Fighter light, buzzes a pilot's cockpit at midnight; he grips the controls, FEARFUL of the glowing thing no radar can explain, and radios for help.

reading_story: Sage leans close to the ledge, counting each wick's trembling beat on his fingers, and declares every private rhythm pure NATURE before it even flickers.

reading_story: Kyo screams into the mic as a girder-heavy sail crashes toward the crowd. Bodies freeze in raw FEAR as the whole stage tips over.

story: On the left, the Listening Ear cups forward and catches a faint echo of its own blunder; on the right, a heart flushes crimson, shrivels small, and burns with SHAME.
reading_story: Chee, the clipped cheerleader, fumbles her pyramid mid-cheer and topples the whole squad; pom-poms scatter, and she cartwheels off the mat into SHAME.

reading_story: A Soaker sponge presses against your ribs, swelling and shrinking with every BREATH until it is heavy and dripping wet.

The meaning-story frame ('watching your chest, breath in the quiet dark') is somewhat archetypal and risks interference with other calm/rest-themed kanji.

story: At the bottom of the ribcage, a heart droops, cracked down the middle, leaking gray tears. Nothing props it up. Utterly, hopelessly SAD.

issues: Borderline (not blocking): 'ribcage' in the main story is not a supplied component — it reads as natural anatomical scenery for the heart (心), and coincidentally aligns with 非's rib-like top shape while reinforcing 心's bottom placement, so it is not treated as a phantom component actor.

Distinctiveness capped at 3: the drooping/crying-heart = sadness image is archetypal for 心-family emotion kanji and risks interference with neighbors sharing the heart component.

reading_story: Joe stares at the Twin Candle Wicks until his throat tightens — Joooe, he groans, dragging the vowel out long, drowning in raw FEELINGS he can't name.

story: Staring inward at nothing, eyes unfocused, you sink beneath thought entirely — until a single CONCEPT surfaces from the quiet dark of your heart, glowing.

issues: meaning_placement is labeled 'end' but CONCEPT is not the literal final word of the story ('...CONCEPT surfaces from the quiet dark of your heart, glowing.') — it's in the climactic clause but followed by a trailing phrase; acceptable as loosely 'end-positioned' but worth tightening in future generations.

issues: Minor: 'doorway' is an invented scene detail not tied to any listed component — acceptable as scenery since it doesn't impersonate a phantom kanji component.

story: Falling Katana slices one clean mark above an Open Mouth crying out; below, a heart pounds while a planted Barbed Pike stands sentinel over it all — pure EMOTION.
reading_story: Genghis Khan roars from his horse, flooded with raw EMOTION as his army cries out behind him.

story: ACCUSTOMED to the ritual, the Twin Candle Wicks flicker on their left ledge while, beside them, a Skewered Sack drops straight down onto a polished Cowrie Shell, the rod ringing the coin-clam like every night before.

reading_story: Sage stands over the newly-slashed pike, stroking his white beard, drawing the sound long: "seeee..." he intones, "it will TURN INTO something else now."

story: A Trailing Mane sweeps down from above; within it a long Trailing Tassel dangles and three Comb Streaks rake through. Below, one muddy Trailing Footprint drags off the flat Horizon Line — salon HAIR OF THE HEAD.

issues: Distinctiveness weakness: three component actors share the 'Trailing' prefix (Trailing Footprint, Trailing Tassel, Trailing Mane) clustered in one story, risking within-story confusability and interference with neighbor kanji that reuse these actors.
The word 'one' (kanji_keyword for 一 / Horizon Line) grammatically attaches to the Footprint ('one muddy Trailing Footprint') rather than the Horizon Line, slightly muddying the 一 = 'one' encoding.

Dense nested decomposition: since 髟 already contains 長 + 彡, the scene stacks five hair-ish trailing/strand elements that can visually blur together, raising cognitive load (imageability held at 4 rather than 5).
